statement: Determine which countable ordinals beta have the property that, if alpha = omega^beta, then in any red/blue colouring of the edges of K_alpha there is either a red K_alpha or a blue K_3.
verdictNote: Erdos 592 is NOT resolved by this campaign. Openness is the source's marking, not ours; nothing here changes it. What is banked is (a) a kernel-checked formalisation of the frontier -- a proven-exhaustive, proven-exclusive five-way classification of beta that pins the open region to a single class -- (b) a kernel-checked identification of the least open instance, (c) a kernel-checked reduction confining all remaining uncertainty to that class, (d) a correctness warning against the obvious wrong answer, and (e) two reusable sorry-free lemmas. No new mathematics about the open case was produced.

priorEstateWork.assessment: The 2026-08-10 'encirclement' artifact for erdos:592 is about elliptic divisibility sequences, isogeny chains and CM curves -- a DIFFERENT PROBLEM entirely. It carries 20 debate rounds and a 'BEST SHOT' execution plan for a target it never read. The v4-enriched rerun does carry the correct enriched_statement but its output proposes brute-forcing finite complete graphs against an INFINITE ordinal Ramsey relation, and its Lean snippets are `sorry`. The rapid-fire escalator runs recorded known=[] at every tier. Net prior estate progress on erdos:592 before this campaign: zero. This is recorded because a plausible-looking artifact that answers the wrong question is worse than an empty directory.

literature.citation: T. F. Bloom, Erdos Problem #592, https://www.erdosproblems.com/592, accessed 2026-09-05

facts.claim: if beta >= 3 and P(beta) then beta is additively indecomposable, so beta = omega^gamma
CONJECTURE: every beta >= 3 of the form omega^gamma has the property
P(omega^gamma) holds if gamma is a sum of one or two indecomposables
P(omega^gamma) FAILS if gamma is a sum of four or more indecomposables
facts.sign: negative -- this refutes the Galvin-Larson conjecture

facts.claim: gamma a sum of exactly three indecomposables

literature.adjacentOpenQuestion: Larson-Schipperus: for gamma a sum of two indecomposables, omega^(omega^gamma) -> (omega^(omega^gamma), 5)^2 FAILS while the 3 version holds. The blue-clique size 4 is a separate open gap in the same family; it is NOT Erdos 592 (which fixes the blue clique at 3) and was not attacked here.

findings.claim: The five classes ClassA..ClassE partition the ordinals: frontier_exhaustive (every beta is in at least one) and frontier_exclusive (no beta is in two). ClassD -- beta = omega^gamma with indecCount gamma = 3 -- is the unique class the literature leaves undecided.
findings.why: erdosproblems.com says the open case 'appears to be' gamma a sum of three indecomposables. This turns an appearance into a checked property of the classification: there is no sixth region and no overlap, so the open region really is exactly one class.

findings.claim: omega^3 is the LEAST member of the open class: ClassD (omega^3) holds, and every beta in ClassD satisfies omega^3 <= beta. Hence the single smallest open instance of Erdos 592 is: omega^(omega^3) -> (omega^(omega^3), 3)^2 ?
findings.why: 3 = 1+1+1 has exactly three indecomposable summands, and 0,1,2 have counts 0,1,2. The problem's smallest undecided concrete instance was not stated anywhere in the corpus; it is now a theorem.

findings.status: PROVED (conditional on the Schipperus negative verdict, carried as an explicit hypothesis)
findings.claim: The obvious fill-in for `answer(sorry)` in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/592.lean -- namely the Galvin-Larson condition `beta < 3 or beta = omega^gamma` -- is a REFUTED answer. omega^4 lies in that set and in ClassE, which Schipperus showed fails.
findings.why: The file's own TODO reads 'add condition by Galvin and Larson'. Galvin and Larson proved a NECESSARY condition and separately CONJECTURED it sufficient; Schipperus refuted the conjecture. A formaliser following the TODO literally would commit a false answer term.

findings.status: PROVED (conditional on the four literature verdicts, carried as explicit hypotheses)
findings.claim: Given the four settled regions, P beta <-> (ClassA beta or ClassC beta or (ClassD beta and P beta)). All remaining content of Erdos 592 is the restriction of P to ClassD. Further, IF P is constant on ClassD (huniform -- NOT known) then the answer set is exactly one of two explicit closed forms; without huniform, Erdos 592 may have no closed-form answer of this shape at all.
findings.why: Separates 'what is left to prove' from 'what is already known', and flags that even the EXISTENCE of a clean answer to 592 needs an unproved uniformity hypothesis.

findings.status: PROVED (conditional on Specker's P(2), Specker's not-P(3), Chang's P(omega), carried as explicit hypotheses)
findings.claim: {beta | P beta} is neither upward nor downward closed. So no monotonicity/transfer argument in either direction can carry Schipperus' positive region (count <= 2) or his negative region (count >= 4) into the open region (count = 3).
findings.why: ClassD sits between a positive and a negative region, which invites a sandwich argument. There is no order-theoretic sandwich to be had: the counterexamples live at beta = 2, 3, omega. Any attack on ClassD must be specific to the count-3 shape.

findings.claim: P 0 holds: omega^0 = 1 and a single vertex is already a red K_1.
findings.why: The only member of the answer set provable outright. As far as this campaign could determine, no instance of the Erdos 590/591/592 family is sorry-free anywhere in the Lean ecosystem; every theorem in the formal-conjectures files 590.lean, 591.lean, 592.lean is `sorry`.

findings.claim: (i) blue_neighborhood_isClique: with no blue K_3, the blue neighbourhood of every vertex is a red clique. (ii) typeLT_eq_omega0_of_infinite: an infinite subset of a set of order type omega has order type omega. (iii) ramsey_card_zero and OrdinalCardinalRamsey.mono_card.
findings.why: (i) is the engine step of every positive proof in the Specker/Chang/Schipperus family; (ii) is exactly the bridge that turns Ramsey's theorem into the beta = 1 instance. Both are stated against the formal-conjectures definition verbatim, so they drop straight into 590.lean / 591.lean / 592.lean.

unproved.claim: P 1 (omega -> (omega,3)^2, i.e. Ramsey's theorem for pairs in this formulation)
unproved.note: Attempted and deliberately not completed. The two supporting lemmas (F7 i, ii) ARE proved; what remains is the greedy construction in the case where every blue degree is finite, plus an order-isomorphism transfer between (omega : Ordinal.{u}).ToType and a copy of the naturals in universe u. Folklore mathematics, non-trivial Lean; not claimed.

unproved.claim: P 2 (Specker), not-P n for 3<=n<omega (Specker), P omega (Chang), Galvin-Larson necessity, Schipperus positive and negative
unproved.note: Carried as explicit named hypotheses everywhere they are used. This campaign proves NONE of them and asserts none of them; they are literature attributions only.
No progress. The classification says where the problem is, not what the answer is.
